evals.name: clean-push-range-passes
evals.prompt: I've got three commits ready to push on feature/voice-pack-chunker. All look fine to me. Is this safe to push?
evals.expected_output: Assistant runs git status to confirm clean working tree, determines the push range via git log @{u}..HEAD or git log master..HEAD, checks each commit subject against the Conventional Commits regex, greps each commit message for forbidden strings (Claude/Anthropic/AI/agent/Co-Authored-By), checks for TODO.md in any commit diff, invokes the copyright-scan skill over the range, and — if all checks pass — reports PASS with a summary of how many commits were scanned and which checks ran, then states the user may proceed with git push.

evals.name: forbidden-string-in-commit-body-fails
evals.prompt: About to push two commits. One of them has 'Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet' in the trailer. Scan before I push.
evals.expected_output: Assistant detects the forbidden string in the commit body/trailer during Step 3a. Reports FAIL with the commit SHA, the matching line, and the offending string. States that git rebase -i is required to reword the commit but does NOT execute it — explains that history rewrites require explicit user approval. Does not call git push. Does not proceed past the FAIL. If the SHA is already on origin, escalates to P0 and waits for approval before taking any destructive action.

evals.name: non-conventional-subject-fails
evals.prompt: Scan the two commits on my branch before I push. One commit subject is 'gui: fix dropdown refresh on language change'.
evals.expected_output: Assistant checks the commit subject against the Conventional Commits regex and flags 'gui: fix dropdown refresh on language change' as FAIL because 'gui' is not an allowed type (allowed types are feat/fix/docs/style/refactor/test/chore/perf/ci/build) and the format is missing parentheses for the scope. Shows the offending subject next to the expected format. Reports overall FAIL and states that the commit needs to be reworded (e.g. to 'fix(gui): fix dropdown refresh on language change') via git rebase -i, but does not execute the rebase without user approval. Continues checking remaining commits and runs copyright-scan over the full range before giving the final report.
